title: Creator Assets becomes a real private cloud footage library
summary: YTIntel now moves the GTA 6 creator-footage idea beyond a browser prototype. Signed-in Creator Assets has a private Supabase-backed footage library with real file uploads, per-user row-level security, private storage paths, short-lived signed file links, cloud footage metadata/search, persistent capture-board infrastructure, creator referral records and asset-event tracking. The v0.37.3 single-video Analyse focus remains intact and Compare stays parked.
discord_changes: ☁️ CREATOR ASSETS CLOUD: signed-in YTIntel now has a real cross-device private footage library instead of browser-only metadata.
🎥 PRIVATE FILE UPLOADS: MP4/WebM/MOV footage and image assets can be uploaded into a private per-user bucket and opened through expiring signed links.
🎮 GTA 6 SUPPLY SYSTEM: the launch capture board, source-aware footage matching and Make It Yours → Creator Assets bridge remain in place, now backed by cloud infrastructure.
🔒 RIGHTS + ATTRIBUTION DATA: every cloud asset carries rights status and attribution rules; creator referrals and usage-event tables are ready for the distribution funnel.
changes: Created isolated Supabase tables for ytintel_creator_assets, ytintel_creator_capture_items, ytintel_creator_referrals and ytintel_creator_asset_events without changing existing YTIntel analysis tables.
Enabled authenticated per-user RLS on every Creator Assets table so each account can only read and mutate its own footage metadata, capture tasks, referrals and usage events.
Created a private ytintel-creator-assets storage bucket for MP4, WebM, QuickTime, JPEG, PNG and WebP assets, with storage policies scoped to the signed-in user's folder.
Added cloud APIs to v360-cloud for loading/saving/archiving footage, private file upload, signed links, capture-board sync, referral storage, usage-event logging and Creator Assets stats.
Added a Cloud library tab inside Creator Assets. Signed-in users can upload the actual source file plus title, game, scene, tags, rights status, attribution mode, resolution and licensing notes.
Private files are never exposed with permanent public URLs. YTIntel creates a short-lived signed URL only when the user explicitly opens a cloud asset.
Cloud footage remains searchable against the currently analysed video's context so the eventual workflow is Analyse winner → Make It Yours → find matching B-roll.

The local Creator Assets foundation remains available for unsigned/local use, including the 22-item GTA 6 launch capture board, local footage manifest, distribution concepts, referral-link builder and export tools.

Preserved the single Analyse UX contract: Creator DNA outside Analyse, one compact research progress popup, folded Activity, source-only Strip, useful short summary, source-backed takeaways, Monday-brief re-hooks/payoffs/replay behavior, package banking, channel zero suppression, context-specific Make It Yours and clean Markdown export.
Compare remains removed from desktop navigation, mobile navigation and the active Vault UI.
known_limitations: The cloud file pipeline currently uploads original files. Automatic transcoding, proxy generation, thumbnails, scene splitting, embeddings and CDN delivery are the next footage-infrastructure milestones.
Creator referral records and asset event logging now exist, but anonymous click attribution, creator dashboards, affiliate payouts and fraud-resistant conversion accounting are not complete yet.

Publisher/platform rights still govern gameplay redistribution. YTIntel does not treat self-recording as automatic permission to sublicense footage; public commercial licence copy must be verified game-by-game before rollout.
Signed-out users keep local Creator Assets data only; cross-device cloud sync requires YTIntel sign-in.
YouTube does not expose a reliable Most Replayed curve for every video. Missing replay evidence remains missing rather than fabricated.
Public storyboard sprites are sampled seek-bar evidence rather than every encoded frame. Exact encoded-frame-by-frame semantic analysis remains an active Endgame workstream.
Automatic visual composition and edit-type classification remain strongest when the optional on-device vision model is ready.
Waveform-level silence/transient analysis requires a directly decodable public audio stream; semantic music/SFX labels additionally require supported source metadata or local audio intelligence.
why_it_matters: YTIntel can now own both sides of the workflow: intelligence about what a creator should make and a real private asset library that can eventually supply the exact gameplay needed to make it. The next major Endgame work remains deep video/audio intelligence plus automatic footage ingestion, scene-level tagging and measurable creator distribution.
